'''Phantom Ship''' (Japanese: {{hl|幽霊船|Yūreisen}} ''Phantom Ship'') is the eleventh chapter of [[Ephraim]]'s route in {{FE8}}.

After completing this chapter, the player is immediately sent into [[Landing at Taizel|the next]]. It is not possible to return to the [[world map]] during the next chapter.

==Plot==
{{main|Phantom Ship/Script}}

When [[Selena (The Sacred Stones)|Selena]] returns to [[Grado]] Keep, Emperor [[Vigarde]] is disappointed that she failed to execute [[Duessel]]. Selena begs for a second chance, and [[Lyon]] gives her a mission to obtain a [[dragonstone]] located in [[Za'albul Marsh]]. Selena gratefully accepts; she choses to renew her oath of service to Vigarde, and leaves for Za'albul Marsh.

On a ship to Grado, [[Myrrh]] observes the sea for the first time; [[Ephraim]] is also sailing for the first time, but feels he must remain calm and attentive as a leader. Ephraim and Myrrh's conversation is interrupted when [[Seth]] notices an unknown ship approaching them with an inhuman crew. On the other ship, [[Riev]] instructs the [[monster]]s to wreak havoc on the ocean.

During the battle, the monsters' ship comes alongside Ephraim's as they board. Later, Ephraim spots another ship in the distance, but cannot identify its crew—on the other ship, [[L'Arachel]] and [[Dozla]] prepare to fight the monsters terrorizing the ocean.

Ephraim can talk to L'Arachel during the battle; Ephraim does not recognize her or tales of her exploits, buts asks for her assistance fighting the monsters, which she is glad to provide. L'Arachel can then talk to Dozla, informing him that they will now be working with Ephraim.

Once the monsters are routed, L'Arachel introduces herself to Ephraim; Ephraim introduces himself as the prince of [[Renais]], and L'Arachel clarifies that she is the princess of [[Rausten]]. Ephraim informs L'Arachel of his mission to Grado, and L'Arachel insists on accompanying him in spite of the dangers; if Dozla is alive, L'Arachel informs him of their new destination, and Dozla unquestioningly accompanies her.

The ships in the map image move into those positions over time.
*At first, the player ship and enemy ship are far apart.
*On turn 2, the enemy ship moves closer to the player ship.
*On turn 3, three plank bridges appear to connect the two ships.
*On turn 5, the NPC ship appears.

====Reinforcements====
*Turn 2
**The enemy ship approaches, bringing the main enemy army of 6 [[Revenant]]s, 12 [[Bonewalker]]s, 1 [[Wight]], and 2 [[Entombed]]
*Turn 3
**2 [[Mogall]]s from the northwest corner of the map
**2 [[Mogall]]s from the southwest corner of the map
*Turns 4–6
**1 [[Bonewalker]] with a [[Steel Lance]] from the upper stairs on the enemy ship
**1 [[Bonewalker]] with a [[Steel Sword]] from the lower stairs on the enemy ship
*Turn 4
**2 [[Gargoyle]]s from the northeast corner of the map
**2 [[Mogall]]s from the southeast corner of the map
*Turn 5
**4 [[Mogall]]s; two from north of the enemy ship, two from south of the enemy ship <small>(Difficult only)</small>
**2 [[Gargoyle]]s with [[Iron Lance]]s from west of the player ship
**1 [[Gargoyle]] with a [[Steel Lance]] from west of the player ship <small>(Difficult only)</small>
**1 [[Gargoyle]] with a [[Javelin]] from west of the player ship <small>(Difficult only)</small>
**The boss [[Deathgoyle]] from west of the player ship

==Strategy==
{{strategy}}
{{sectstub}}
This chapter is significantly harder on Difficult mode due to the sheer amount of enemies with high stats for this point of the game. This also makes recruiting L'Arachel very hard due to her low durability. It is highly recommended to deploy promoted units such as Seth and Duessel for this chapter.

==Trivia==
*This chapter, alongside [[Creeping Darkness]], was possibly one of the last chapters added to the game in development, being the only two chapters completely absent from the prototype. This may also be the reason it does not have a corresponding world map location, instead occurring between locations, as the world map was already laid out in essentially its final form even in the very early prototype.
**This fact is also supported by the fact that Creeping Darkness and Phantom Ship are the only two chapters with their titles listed out of order, being at the end of the list, internally.
